target_customer: Gamers and teams needing voice chat
problem: Ventrilo, TeamSpeak and Mumble required downloading clients and entering server addresses and ports.
business_model: Free beta; planned paid tiers at about half competitors' price

founders.name: Andrew Ow
founders.background_notes: YC page says he founded Haiku Games and previously cofounded Voxli

competitors.name: Vivox
competitors.what: Game voice provider announcing a cross platform browser plugin

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser plugin with push to talk hotkeys, 200 user rooms and cross platform support in 2009; audio mixing and plugin work were nontrivial.

defensibility.rationale: No restricted rooms at launch, no lock in, and Vivox was entering the same wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Vivox moved to a browser plugin in March 2009 and was later bought by Unity in 2019; no Voxli buyer is recorded.

market_need_then: Gamers needed voice chat in games and teams; the incumbents were considered clumsy to set up, which TechCrunch cited in March 2009.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches for name origin, logo, mascot, rebrands and press about the brand returned nothing about this company, so the brand is rated at the floor on absence of evidence only. The name seems built on the Latin vox, but no source says so.

outcome_analysis: Voxli launched in March 2009 with free browser group voice chat and a plan to charge half the price of incumbents. It had restricted room gaps and faced Vivox and entrenched desktop tools. CB Insights marks it dead with the YC amount only, and no shutdown cause is public; the factors are inferences.
notes: voxli.com returned HTTP 503. $20K round from CB Insights only, undated. Failure factors inferred, shutdown cause not public.
